Every touch for Mason Greenwood, playing his first game in England since January 2022, was booed, but even louder applause was reserved for Aston Villa’s rediscovered attacking prowess. The major surprise was how the hosts managed to score three. Iraola’s pre-match faith in the big-money signings Barcola and Florian Wirtz was repaid as the pair helped dismantle limited opponents. quietus.title: Long Nights in the Sound Forest: Highlights from Skaņu Mežs 2026
quietus.description: Daryl Worthington returns to Latvia’s Skaņu Mežs, where sets from Cities Aviv, KMRU, Sophia Djebel Rose and more provide a much-needed sonic salve Sofi, photo by Artūrs Pavlovs It’s deep into the closing night of Skaņu Mežs 2026 and Cities Aviv, aka Wilbert Gavin Mays, is on the edge of the stage pointing insistently through the darkness at the speakers and urging the sound technicians to turn them up. They comply, lifting his beats even louder so that, from my point close to the stage in the cavernous main hall of Riga’s Hanzas Perons, his chopped and screwed tracks coagulate into an all-consuming ripple of sound, seeping through my ears, into my brain, and on to vibrating in overlapping…

quietus.title: Heroína – Heroína
quietus.description: Heroína Heroína Someone has pissed these lads off, and we’re all the richer for it Heroína by Heroína ‘Corre’ means run. On this opener, Heroína do. No count-in, no settling, Vasco Galvão’s blast beats already at full pelt by the time you’ve registered it’s started and Martim Fernandes flying halfway up the neck. It lasts sixty-four seconds. The other twenty-two minutes are more of the same, which I mean as highest praise. ‘Escarro’ at least has a theme, a tumbling three-note figure that could’ve fallen off a Polvo record or a Don Caballero one (newly reunited, mercifully), before the whole show capsizes into bayou-thick Eyehategod sludge and Dillinger Escape Plan’s jackknifing chord…

quietus.title: Combined Worlds: Kali Malone’s Favourite Albums
quietus.description: From early modern Renaissance compositions, through 20th century minimalism, all the way to grunge, Kali Malone treats Claire Biddles to a centuries-spanning Baker's Dozen Photo by Kingsley Ifill Kali Malone has always kept a home in several musical worlds at once. When she was 18, studying at the Royal College Of Music in Stockholm, she would make regular visits to her hometown of Denver, Colorado, diving back into the metal scene in which she was embedded as a teenager. “I was basically living part-time in Sweden, part-time in a metal house in Denver,” she recalls from her present-day Paris apartment. “I was studying electroacoustic composition, but I also wanted to engage with the metal…

quietus.title: Jon Hassell – Music Is Invisible (Pentimento Volume Three)
quietus.description: Jon Hassell Music Is Invisible (Pentimento Volume Three) A final album from the Memphis-born trumpet player and composer Music Is Invisible (Pentimento Volume Three) by Jon Hassell Jon Hassell departed this world on 26th June 2021. He’d lived an extraordinary life entwined in the musical landscape of the 20th century, studying under Stockhausen and Pandit Pran Nath, and collaborating with the likes of Terry Riley, La Monte Young, Brian Eno, Talking Heads, Techno Animal, David Sylvian, Björk and Ry Cooder. He also developed the highly influential concept of Fourth World music, a blend of primitive and futuristic ideas and techniques encompassing modern electronic sounds and global…

quietus.title: JD Twitch’s Record Collection to be Sold
quietus.description: World Of Echo to sell 20,000 records belonging to the late Optimo lynchpin JD Twitch portrait by Marissa Costello The death of Keith McIvor – AKA JD Twitch – a year ago was a huge loss to the music community of which The Quietus is a part, a DJ, figurehead and inspiration to music fans, obsessives, musicians, dancers, artists, writers all over the world. Now, the thousands of records that made him, and that formed the raw materials of his sets with Optimo and beyond, are to be sold. They'll head off to find new lives in new record collections via a sale at the World Of Echo record shop on Cheshire Street, London, with each vinyl record cleaned, graded and featuring...

Following drummer Jason Roeder’s unceremonious sacking in 2024, it appears Matt Pike is also out of the band now too, with rumours running rife as to what could have prompted the shirtless axeman to leave – when the new iteration of the band dropped their first single ‘Have Spacesuit Will Travel’ back in June, most…

quietus.title: Institut Für Feinmotorik – Öd
quietus.description: Institut Für Feinmotorik Öd Black Forest experimental turntablists return with a new album for the Faitiche label Öd by Institut fuer Feinmotorik Another week, another tech bro triumphantly declaring music solved, with hyper-individualisation via AI just around the corner. This obnoxious class of talentless grifters is obsessed with optimising everything, art included, and misses the point entirely. We want – no, need! – art to be messy, incomplete, and flawed. Take Institut Für Feinmotorik, originally from Germany’s Black Forest. The collective have spent years paring their sound down to squeaking, sparse forms that sound like mechanical contraptions in their death throes, indebted to…

quietus.title: Life is Death: An Interview with Róis
quietus.description: On Mo Léan, Róis uses the ancient art of keening and otherworldly electronics to challenge the foundations of what we consider to be ‘proper’ when it comes to death. Here, she speaks to Deirdre Anna Rose Kelly about grief for a nation as well as individuals, the complexities of outsiders’ romanticisation of Irish culture, and the role of the Irish language in her work Photos by Anthony O'Connor “I want to party and to have the craic. That’s where I’m at,” says Róis. To the casual observer, this desire for fun might seem at odds with the work at hand. The title of her critically lauded last album, Mo Léan, newly reissued and expanded for its first global release by Domino next...

aquariumdrunkard.title: PAINT :: Whip of an Ear
aquariumdrunkard.description: No one is making music quite like PAINT, the project of musician and Allah-Las guitarist Pedrum Siadatian. If a song title can be prophetic, it's "Illusion of Voice" here, in which the vocals of real and hypothetical cast of ensemble characters and collaborators weave through a shadowy labyrinth full of twists of surrealistic transparency. From police blotter audio soundscapes to warbled poetry reads, fourth record Whip of an Ear is an obtusely captivating listen and one of the prolific musician's best offerings yet.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Piero Umiliani :: Il Corpo
aquariumdrunkard.description: Piero Umiliani’s Il Corpo is the sound of something beautiful beginning to sour. Released in 1974, the soundtrack finds the Italian composer in familiar aesthetic territory, where jazz, funk, psychedelia and library music bleed into one another. Sunny music for shady people, it embodies the anything-goes spirit of Italian library music, spinning a parallel film from grooves, fuzz and atmosphere.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Transmissions :: Richard Thompson (2026)
aquariumdrunkard.description: Hippies, Thugs, and Heroes finds guitarist Richard Thompson sounding as savage, lyrical, and eloquent as ever. This week on Aquarium Drunkard Transmissions, we're pleased to welcome Thompson back to the show. If you dig Transmissions, there’s a pretty solid chance that you already know that he's one of the founding fathers of British folk rock, known for his work with Fairport Convention, Sandy Denny, his former wife Linda Thompson, Nick Drake and others.

aquariumdrunkard.title: The Lagniappe Sessions :: Beefheart & McQuinn
aquariumdrunkard.description: Beefheart & McQuinn’s Midtown Downtime arrived earlier this year as a ten-song distillation of folk-rock’s softer, more unhurried pleasures. Think. close harmonies, crisp arrangements, and an easygoing, J.J. Cale-like sway. For their Lagniappe Session, William Murray and Winter McQuinn turn to three favorites from their record collections: Danny O’Keefe’s “The Road,” Mark Fry’s “Song For Wilde,” and Heron’s “Lord & Master.” Spanning road-worn singer-songwriter fare and the pastoral reaches of British folk, the selections share the qualities that animate the duo’s own work.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Sunlight/Water :: A Skygreen Leopards Sampler
aquariumdrunkard.description: Fog lifting off San Francisco’s Victorian rooftops, twelve-string guitars catching the morning light, and the ghost of a California that exists somewhere between memory and myth. A curated sampler spanning Skygreen Leopards’ 2001–2014 catalogue, tracing Glenn Donaldson and Donovan Quinn’s journey from lo-fi jangle-psych fragments to sun-dappled pop reveries—an overlooked gem of the Bay Area underground, steeped in eucalyptus hillsides, coastal haze, and the strange, enduring magic of the West Coast.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Offworlding: Ambient House, 1992-1997 (A Mixtape)
aquariumdrunkard.description: For a fleeting moment in the early-to-mid 90s, ambient house consummated the perfect synthesis of dance music groove and cosmic expanse. Emerging from the chillout rooms and the afterparties at the margins of club culture, ambient house cultivated the psychedelic elements of the rave scene into an altogether more atmospheric direction. The scene produced a handful of genuine superstars in the Orb and the Future Sound of London, but beneath these, there lies a whole galaxy of trippy, pulsing electronica to traverse. Here are a few hours to get you started.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Axis: Sova :: Flowerage
aquariumdrunkard.description: Chicago guitarist Brett Sova slips further from psychedelic overload and closer to new wave song structure in this fifth full-length. This second album with a full band—Sova himself, plus bassist Jeremy Freeze and drummer Josh Johannpeter—layers clean, warbly guitar texture with sawtoothed bass, sounding, at intervals, like a brighter, more optimistic Wipers.

aquariumdrunkard.title: CAN :: Karussell der Jugend, Soest 1970
aquariumdrunkard.description: No blueprint. Filmed by West German television in November 1970 at the Karussell der Jugend festival in Soest, this 84-minute document captures CAN with Damo Suzuki, Michael Karoli, Irmin Schmidt, Holger Czukay and Jaki Liebezeit, still exploring the possibilities of a sound that didn't quite resemble anything else. Repetition, interruption, groove and collective instinct. More than half a century later, the footage preserves the band before their influence had been mapped and their sound codified, when the music was still mutating in real time.

Wearing violet, she bows low to the floor and begs Okatsu, who manages the house, for permission to leave. When Élisabeth was released to blanket disinterest, Scherer began to branch out from literature into film criticism, and, later, filmmaking. With each new endeavor, the pseudonyms piled up.
